                        </ns0:gap>kels</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Sanctuary,</ns0:hi> which being but of the value of two Shillings six pence apiece amount<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed but to 3. <ns0:hi>l.</ns0:hi> 15. <ns0:hi>s.</ns0:hi> o. in our Money, which was the Sum ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pointed by the Law, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 21.32. to be paid for a <ns0:hi>Servant, gored to Death by the Beast of another,</ns0:hi> the poorest and meanest price of any Persons Life, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> left it to them and they set the meanest price imaginable. There are other opinions about the value of these pieces of Silver, but this is the most probable, especially considering the mean opinion these Men had of Christ, and their design and interest to depreciate him as much as might be, and that the <ns0:hi>Priests</ns0:hi> were the great Men in this Coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cil, who most probably agreed with him for such pieces of Mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ney as were mo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t in use amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>; It may be a just matter of Admiration, that they should make so Cheap a Bar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gain with him<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> considering that they doubtless (had he insisted upon it) would have given him more, but there was a Prophe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sy to be fulfilled, which we find, <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 11. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 12. <ns0:hi>So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of Silver. And the Lord said to me, cast it to the Potter. A good<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>y price that I was prized at of them.</ns0:hi> I shall have occasion when I come to <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 27.9. to dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />course that Text further. The price was set by the Council of Heaven, which had determined this Degree of our Lords Humi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />liation, that as he took upon him the form of a Servant, so his Life should be valued at the rate of an ordinary Servants Life. Tho therefore <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> was covetous enough to have asked more, and it is like the malice of those Councellors, would have edged them to have given more, yet it was thus ordered by the Divine Coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cil. Christ must be sold Cheap, that he might be the more dear to the Souls of the redeemed ones; for <ns0:hi>thirty pieces of Silver</ns0:hi> he Covenanted with them, and they promised it to him; whether it was now paid, or when he had done his work, appeareth not. <ns0:hi>From that time</ns0:hi> (saith <ns0:hi>Matthew) he sought how he might conveniently</ns0:hi> betray him. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> expounds this <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out Tumult, Ch.</ns0:hi> 22.6. He was now fixedly resolved upon his Vil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lany, his <ns0:hi>Lust</ns0:hi> wanted but opportunity, which soon after offer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed it self.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 Now the first <ns0:hi>day</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>feast</ns0:hi> of unleaven<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed bread, the disciples came to <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>esus, saying unto him, Where wilt thou that we prepare for thee to eat the passover?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 And he said, Go into the city to such a man, and say unto him, The master saith, My time is at hand: I will keep the passover, at thy house with my disciples.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 And the disciples did as Jesus had appointed them, and they made ready the passover.<ns0:note place="bottom">No one of the Evangelists relates this History fully, but <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> relateth the former part more fully than <ns0:hi>Matthew, Mar.</ns0:hi> 14.12<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 13, 14, 15, 16. And the first day <ns0:hi>of unleavened Bread, when they killed the Passover; his Disciples said unto him, W<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ere wilt thou, that we go and prepare that thou mayst eat the Passover? And he sendeth forth two of his Disciples, and saith unto them, Go ye into the City, and there shall meet you a Man bearing a Pitcher of Water, follow him: And wheresoever he shall go in, say you to the good Man of the House, The Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ster saith, where is the Guest-Chamber, where I shall Eat the Passover with my Disciples? And he shall shew you a large upper Room furnished, and prepared, there make ready for us. And his Disciples went forth, and came into the City, and found as he had said unto them, and they made ready the Passover. Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 22.7, 8, 9, &c. differeth a little in the former part of this Relation: He saith, <ns0:hi>Then came the day of unleavened Bread, when the Passover must be killed. And he sent Peter and Iohn, saying, Go, and prepare the Passover, that we may Eat: And they said unto him, where wilt thou, that we prepare? And he said unto them: Behold, when you are entred into the City, there shall a Man meet you,</ns0:hi> &c. So he goeth on, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 10, 11, 12. varying scarce at all from what <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith. The Variati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons of the Evangelists are of no moment, none contradicteth the other, only one hath some Circumstances omitted by the o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther. Our Lord was now at <ns0:hi>Bethany,</ns0:hi> whither he went every Night from <ns0:hi>Ierusalem.</ns0:hi> The day was come for <ns0:hi>the killing of the Passover.</ns0:hi> What that day was, the Law hath fixed, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 12.6. <ns0:hi>The Fourteenth day of the first Month (Nisan)</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Evening:</ns0:hi> Or, betwixt the two <ns0:hi>Evenings.</ns0:hi> (That is, as is mostly agreed) betwixt the declining of the Sun after noon, and the setting of the Sun; for they counted <ns0:hi>one Evening</ns0:hi> began when the Sun was declined, which was the second Evening of that day, and another Evening (belonging to the insuing day) be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ginning at Sun-set. Betwixt these <ns0:hi>two Evenings, the Passover was</ns0:hi> to be killed; now this Fourteenth day, was called <ns0:hi>The first day of unleavened Bread,</ns0:hi> tho strictly it was not so, according to the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Account of days, from Sun-set to Sun-set; but it was so after the <ns0:hi>Roman Account,</ns0:hi> who count the days as we do, from <ns0:hi>Midnight to Midnight:</ns0:hi> For the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> began their Feast of <ns0:hi>unleavened Bread, from their Eating the Passover:</ns0:hi> So as their Fourteenth day, must needs take in so many Hours as were betwixt the setting of the Sun, and Midnight, of the first day of unleavened Bread, which held to the end of the twenty first day. So were seven entire days with a part of another. <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mark,</ns0:hi> bring in the Disciples <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>rst, asking our Saviour, (knowing his resolution to keep the Passover) <ns0:hi>where he would have it prepared?</ns0:hi> He said (<ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith) to <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iohn<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Go into the City to such a Man,</ns0:hi> &c. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> here, supply something omitted by <ns0:hi>Matthew,</ns0:hi> for <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> only mentioneth their going to the <ns0:hi>Master of the House,</ns0:hi> and telling him from Christ, <ns0:hi>The Master saith my time is at Hand, I will keep the Passover at thy House with my Disciples.</ns0:hi> The other two <ns0:hi>Evangelists</ns0:hi> mention more in their Instructions; telling us that he told th<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, that when they c<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>me into the City, <ns0:hi>They should see a Man carrying a Pitcher of Water,</ns0:hi> whom they should follow into what House soever he should go in, and there they should say to the Master of the House. <ns0:hi>The Master saith my time is at Hand. I will keep the Passover at thy House with my Disciples. Mark</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> add, where is the <ns0:hi>Guest-Cham<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ber?</ns0:hi> No doubt, but at that time most Housholders, who had convenient Houses did prepare <ns0:hi>Chambers,</ns0:hi> for the several <ns0:hi>Passover Companies.</ns0:hi> Our Lord here gave his Disciples an eminent Proo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> of his Divine Nature, in so particularly telling them, what they should meet with in the City; and disposing the Heart of this Housholder, to so free a reception of him. For all three Evangelists agree, <ns0:hi>That the Disciples did as Iesus commanded, and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> as he had said unto them, and they made ready the Passover.</ns0:hi> There was a great deal of work to be done; of which none of the <ns0:hi>Evangelists</ns0:hi> say any thing. Some upon the reading of this, may be thinking. <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> they had the Lamb? W<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>en wa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> it offered?</ns0:hi> &c. According to the Law, in <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 12.3. the L<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>mb was to be taken up the Tenth day, and kept to the Fourteenth; it might either be brought by those that did Eat it, or bought at <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> for they had great Markets for that purpose, some days before the Pa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sover: <ns0:hi>Whether all the Lambs</ns0:hi> thus eaten, by the <ns0:hi>Paschal Societies,</ns0:hi> were first to be brought to the <ns0:hi>Temple,</ns0:hi> and then killed, and the Blood sprinkled on the <ns0:hi>Altar,</ns0:hi> and poured out at the Foot of it, and their Fat and En<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />trails offered, I much doubt; I rather think, this was only to be done with some of them, instead of all. That some were so killed by the Priests, their Blood so sprinkled and poured out upon, and at the Foot of the Altar, I doubt not, tho God ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving no Temple, nor Altar built at that time, there be no such thing in the Law, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 12. but at <ns0:hi>Hezekiah's</ns0:hi> Passover, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 30.16, 17. we find the <ns0:hi>Levites killing the Passover,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Priests sprinkling the Blood</ns0:hi>; but as I said before, I do not think, that the <ns0:hi>Priests</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Levites</ns0:hi> killed the Lambs for all the <ns0:hi>Passover Societies</ns0:hi>: The gre<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t time that it must have taken, and the vast quantity of Blood would have been, the long time it must have taken to cleanse the Entrails<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> makes it appear impossible to be done in four or five hours, for they had no longer time to kill it in. They did not begin to kill till after the Evening Sacrifice, for the day was done with, and that was betwixt two and three of the Clock, and they were to finish by <ns0:hi>Sun-set,</ns0:hi> for then the other Evening began: This inclineth me to think, that every Lamb, was not so killed and offered, only some instead of all. But what the Disciples did as to these matters, the Scripture hath not told us. It is enough for us that we are told the Passover was made ready, and we may be assured, that nothing in the pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />paring of it was omitted, which by the Law of God was re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quired as to this sacred Action. It was not the business of the Evangelists to acquaint us with every particular Circumstance, on<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly to let us know that our Lord did keep the <ns0:hi>Passover,</ns0:hi> and in the close of that Feast institute his Supper, to which Relation our E<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vangelist now comes.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:268" />20 Now when the even was come, he sate down with the twelve.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 And as they did eat, he said. Verily I say un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to you, that one of you shall betray me.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 And they were exceeding sorrowful, and be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gan every one of them to say unto him, Lord is it I?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 And he answered, and said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 41.9.</ns0:note> He that dip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />peth his hand with me in the dish, the same shall betray me.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 The Son of man goeth as it is written of him, but woe unto the man, by whom the Son of man is betrayed, it had been good for that man if he had not been born.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 Then Judas which betrayed him, answered, and said, Master is it I? He said unto hm. Thou hast said.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 17, 18, 19, 20, 21. <ns0:hi>And in the Evening he cometh with the twelve. And as they sate and did Eat. Iesus saith, Verily I say unto you, one of you shall betray me which Eateth with me. And they began to be sorrowful, and to say unto him, one by one, is it I? And he answered and said, It is one of the twelve, that dippeth with me in the Dish. The Son of Man indeed goeth, as it is written of him, but Woe unto that Man, by whom the Son of Man is betrayed; good were it for that Man if he had never been Born. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 22.14, 15, 16, &c. <ns0:hi>And when the Hour was come, he sate down, and the twelve Apostles with him. And he said unto them, with desire have I desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer, for I say unto you, I will not any more eat thereof until it be fulfilled in the Kingdom of God. And he took the Cup and gave thanks, and said, Take this, and divide it <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> your selves. For I say unto you, I will not drink of the Fruit of the Vine, until the Kingdom of God shall come.</ns0:hi> Then <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> passeth to our Lords institution of the <ns0:hi>Supper: Luke</ns0:hi> mixeth the Discourse about the Person that should betray him, with the Relation about the Institu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of the Supper, contrary to the Relation both of <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mark,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> so as we may reasonably think, that <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> mis-placeth it, giving us an Account of that passage, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 21, 22, 23. within his Relation of the History of his receiving the Passover, and instituting of the Supper, which immediately followed each other, but not strictly in that Order, in which our Saviour spake them, which appeareth plainly by the other three Evangelists, to have been during the Eating of the Passover, and before the Institution of the Lords Supper. For the understanding of the History, we must understand some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing of the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Order, in their Eating of the Passover; which was this, as we have it described, by the Learned Doctor <ns0:hi>Lightfoot.</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:q>Their sitting at Meat was commonly upon Beds or Couches, made for that purpose, with the Table before them: Now at other meats, they either sate as we do, with their Bodies erect, or when they would inlarge themselves to more Freedom of Feasting, or refreshing, they sate upon the Beds, and leaned upon the Table on their left Elbow, and this, or the others posture, they used indifferently at other times, as they were disposed, but on the Passover night they thought they were obliged to use this leaning Composure, and you may take their Reason for it in some of their own Words. They used their leaning posture as Free-men do, in memorial of their Freedom. And <ns0:hi>Levi</ns0:hi> said, because it is the manner of Servants, to eat standing, therefore now they Eat sitting, and leaning, to shew that they were got out of Servitude into Free<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom—Upon this Principle and Conceit of Freedom, they used this manner of discumbency, frequently, at other times, but indispensably this Night, so far different from the posture enjoyned and practised at the first Passover in <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> when they ate it with their Loyns girded, their shooes on their Feet, their Staves in their Hands, and in hast, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 12.11. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> And as the thought of their Freedom disposed them to this leaning, reposed, secure Composure of their Elbow upon the Table, and their Head leaning on their Hand, so to Emblem out the Matter the more highly, they laid their Legs under them sitting on them, and laying out their Feet behind them.</ns0:q>
(Thus the Woman, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 7.38. could conveniently come at our Saviours Feet to wash, anoint and wipe them.)
<ns0:q>Thus removing, and acquitting their Legs and Feet, as far as possible, from the least shew of standing to attend, or readiness to go upon any ones imployment, which might carry with it the least Colour of servitude, or Contrariety to their Freedom. Now according to the manner of sitting, and leaning are the Texts to be understood, about the beloved Disciples leaning in the Bosom of Jesus, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 13.23. and on the Breast of Jesus, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 13.25. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 21.20. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                           <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>, or <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                           <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>, which some Translators, not having observed, or at least not expressed, they have intricated the <ns0:hi>Reader,</ns0:hi> in such gross Conceptions about this matter, as that some have thought, and some have pictured <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> reposing himself, or lolling on the Breast of Jesus, contrary to all Order and De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cency: Whereas the manner of sitting together, was only thus, Jesus leaning upon the Table with his left Elbow, and so turn<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing his Face and Breast away from the Table, on one side: <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> sate in the same posture next before him, with his Back towards Jesus, his Breast or Bosom not so neer as that <ns0:hi>Iohns</ns0:hi> Back and Jesus his Breast did joyn together, and touch one another, but at such a distance, as that there was space for Jesus to use his right hand upon the Table, to reach his Meat at his Pleasure, and so for all the rest, as they sate in like manner. For it is but a <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>tange Fancy, with which some have satisfied them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves about this Matter, conceiving either, that they lay upon the Beds before the Table, one tumbling upon, or before the Breast of another, or if they sate leaning on the Table, that they sate so close, that the Back of one joyned to the Breast of another, they sate leaning but with such distance between each other, that the right Hand of every one of them had Li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />berty to come, and go, betwixt himself and his Fellow, to reach his Meat<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> as he had occasion.</ns0:q>—Thus far that Learned Man in his Discourse of the <ns0:hi>Temple-Service, in the time of our Saviour, Ch.</ns0:hi> 13. By which Discourse we may learn. 1. That the Jews at the eating of the Passover, used the very same posture as at other times they did Eat their Meat in. 2. That this was not lying along, but sitting upon their Legs, and sometimes leaning their Head upon their left Elbow, yet at such a distance one from another, as every one that sate might freely use their Right Hand to take their Meat, and reach it to their Mouths: Nor did they always sit at Meat so leaning<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but at their pleasure Leaned, or not Leaned, only at the <ns0:hi>Paschal Supper</ns0:hi> they always Leaned, as an Emblem of their more perfect Liberty. By this we easily understand what is Meant by Christs <ns0:hi>Sitting down with the Twelve,</ns0:hi> after the manner of that Country in eating their Meat. <ns0:hi>And as they did Eat, he said unto them.</ns0:hi> For the understanding of this we must a little inquire into the Jewish manner of Eating that holy Sup<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />per, which I will take out of the afore-mentioned Learned <ns0:hi>Au<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thor</ns0:hi> in the same Book and Chapter, Paragraph third.
<ns0:q>They being thus set the first thing towards this Passover Supper, that they went about, was, that they every one Drank off a Cup of Wine.</ns0:q>
So do their own Directories and Rituals about this thing inform us.—Now the consideration of this is of mighty use to us to help us to understand the two Cups mentioned by <ns0:hi>Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 22. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 17. and again <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 20. The latter was the Cup which our Saviour consecrated for the institution of his Supper, as is plain by the Consecration of the Bread mentioned imme<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />diately before it, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 19. The Cup mentioned, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 17. was their first Cup of Wine, which they Drank before the Passover Sup<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />per, mentioned by <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> only. Our Saviours giving thanks when he took it, was but his <ns0:hi>Blessing</ns0:hi> of the whole <ns0:hi>Paschal Supper. Luke</ns0:hi> before this mentions some Words of our Saviour, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 15, 16. <ns0:hi>with desire have I desired to Eat this Passover with you before I suffer. For I say unto you, I will not Eat any more thereof, until it be fulfilled in the Kingdom of God.</ns0:hi> That is, I am now about to suffer, I know that I am betrayed, I have therefore earnestly desired to Eat this <ns0:hi>Passover</ns0:hi> with you before I dye, to put an end to this Legal Service, which hath now con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tinued so many Years, and hath all this time been but a Type of me, and my Death, and <ns0:hi>Oblation for Sin, Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.29. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 5.7. For this is the <ns0:hi>last Passover</ns0:hi> I shall Eat with you, or that you shall Eat before you see those things fulfilled in Gospel Providences, which this Service doth but Typify. This indeed was but the Preface to the <ns0:hi>Paschal Supper,</ns0:hi> nor doth <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion more of it, only addeth <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 18. <ns0:hi>For I will not Drink of the Fruit of the Vine, until the Kingdom of God shall come.</ns0:hi> Of which Words I shall here say nothing, for they are doubtless by <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> put out of the true order, being both by <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> mentioned, as spoken after that our Saviour had Bles<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sed, and taken the Sacramental Cup. So as questionless the 21, 22. Verses in <ns0:hi>Luke,</ns0:hi> should have been before the eighteenth, accord<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to the order in which <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> patteth them, and <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 18, should be put after <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 20. and so also both <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> do place them. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> mentioneth no more of the <ns0:hi>Paschal</ns0:hi> Supper, let us therefore return to our Evangelist. [<ns0:hi>And as they did Eat</ns0:hi>] that is, the Paschal Supper, which (accord<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to the Law) <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 12.8. was the <ns0:hi>Lamb,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Kid</ns0:hi> roasted, which they were to <ns0:hi>Eat with unleavened Bread, and bitter Herbs.</ns0:hi> The Jews had an hundred Traditional Rites, which they obser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ved about the <ns0:hi>Paschal Supper</ns0:hi> But there seems to have none of them been of any Divine Institution. The Law required no more then the Eating of the Lamb, or Kid roasted, with <ns0:hi>un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />leavened Bread, and bitter Herbs</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> As to their Drink it pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />scribed nothing, they were left to Liberty; for their Tradition of <ns0:hi>four Cups of Wine to be Drank.</ns0:hi> &c. I cannot find any of the Evangelists mentioning our Saviours usage of any such thing, but very probably, he Drank Wine at his Pleasure, as at other Meals. Keeping only to the Rule of the Law. Now saith <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mark. And as they did Eat<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> he said Verily, I say unto you, that one of you shall Betray me.</ns0:hi> He had before told them the <ns0:hi>Son of Man should be betrayed, Ch.</ns0:hi> 17.22. <ns0:hi>&.</ns0:hi> 20.18. where he had also told them he should be <ns0:hi>Scourged, Mocked,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Cru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cified</ns0:hi>; but he now cometh to discover the Traytor to them. <ns0:hi>One of you: And they were exceeding sorrowful, and began every one to say unto him, Lord! Is it I?</ns0:hi> they were sorrowful that he should be Betrayed by any, but more troubled, that one of themselves should be so Accursed an Instrument, every one mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />strusts his own Heart, and <ns0:hi>saith, is it I</ns0:hi>? Christ replyeth, <ns0:hi>He that dippeth his Hand with me in the Dish, the same shall be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tray me.</ns0:hi> The Dish here could be no other, than the <ns0:hi>Dish at the Passover Supper,</ns0:hi> probably the Hand of <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> was at that time with our Saviours in the Dish, for we Read of no more re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ply from any, but from <ns0:hi>Iudas.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour addeth, <ns0:hi>The Son of Man goeth as it is Written of him, but woe unto that Man, by whom the Son of Man is betrayed. It had been good for that Man, if he had not been Born.</ns0:hi> By these Words our Saviour doom<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth the <ns0:hi>Traytor,</ns0:hi> tho withal he tells them, That for his suffering he was determined by God, foretold by the Prophets, and so Eventually necessary, he was not dragged to it, <ns0:hi>the Son of Man goeth.</ns0:hi> But Gods Decree as to the thing, did neither take away the Liberty of <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> his Will in Acting, nor yet excuse the Fact he did. <ns0:hi>Woe unto that Man by whom the Son of Man is be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />trayed.</ns0:hi> A Text worthy of their Study, who will not under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand how God should Decree to permit Sin, and make a sinful Act as to the Event necessary, without being the <ns0:hi>Author of Sin.</ns0:hi> As to our Saviours Death, God had determined it, foretold it, it was necessary to be, but yet Satan put the Evil Motion into the Heart of <ns0:hi>Iudas,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> acted freely in the doing what he did. <ns0:hi>Then</ns0:hi> Judas <ns0:hi>which betrayed him, answered, and said, Master is it I? and he said unto him, Thou hast said.</ns0:hi> This (as I said) maketh it very probable that the Hand of <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> was in the Dish with our Saviours, dipping in the Sauce, when our Saviour spake these former Words. That <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> as well as the other Disciples was with our Lord at this Action, is out of doubt. That he stayed any longer, may very well be question<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, not only because <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 13.30. <ns0:hi>He then having received the Sop, went immediately out.</ns0:hi> But because one can<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />not in reason think that his Guilty Conscience, should suffer him to stay beyond that Word, or that our Saviour would have admitted of the Society of so Prodigious a Traytor at his last Supper, the Institution of which immediately followed-</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:268" />26 And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Many,</ns0:hi> Gr. <ns0:hi>Copies have, given thanks.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> blessed <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> and brake <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> and gave <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> to the dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciples, and said, Take eat this is my body.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and gave <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> to them, saying, Drink ye all of it.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 For this is my blood of the new Testa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, which is shed for many <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">C<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ap. 20.28. Rom. 5.15.</ns0:note> for the remission of sins.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 But I say unto you, I will not drink hence<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />forth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my fathers king<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 And when they had sung an <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> hymn they went out into the mount of olives.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> relates this with no considerable difference, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14. 22, 23, 24, 25, 26. only he saith. <ns0:hi>They drank all of it,</ns0:hi> and—<ns0:hi>shed for many for the Remission of Sins. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, our Saviour upon his giving the Bread, said, <ns0:hi>This is my Body which is given for you. This do in Remembrance of me. Likewise also the Cup after Supper, saying, This Cup is the New Te<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stament in my Blood, which is shed for you.</ns0:hi> From the 24 Verse also to the 33 of his 22. <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> he gives us some further Discourses of our Saviour with <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> and to his Disciples, but no other <ns0:hi>Evangelist</ns0:hi> mentioning them in this place, and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> no where saying that they were spoken in the <ns0:hi>Guest-Chamber,</ns0:hi> I shall not consider them till I come to that Chapter in <ns0:hi>Luke. And as they were Eating,</ns0:hi> that is, while they were yet in the Guest-Chamber, where they had eaten the <ns0:hi>Paschal Lamb</ns0:hi> (for we must not think that our Saviour interrupted them in their very Act of Eating the <ns0:hi>Paschal Lamb,</ns0:hi> with these Words, and another Institution) <ns0:hi>Iesus took Bread,</ns0:hi> without doubt <ns0:hi>unleavened Bread,</ns0:hi> for this Night there was no other to be found in the House of any Jew, nor yet for seven Days which began from the Sun-set of this Night. But it will not from hence follow, that the Lords Supper must be Eaten with unleavened Bread. For tho our Saviour be to be imitated, in his Actions relating to <ns0:hi>Gospel Worship</ns0:hi>; yet not in such of them which had a plain Reference to the <ns0:hi>Iewish Worship,</ns0:hi> and were there instituted for a special reason, as unleavened Bread was, to put them in mind of the hast in which they came out of <ns0:hi>Egypt.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour at this time could use no other than <ns0:hi>unleavened Bread,</ns0:hi> for no other was to be had. <ns0:hi>And blessed it.</ns0:hi> He did not only <ns0:hi>give Thanks</ns0:hi> to God for it, and <ns0:hi>beg his Blessing</ns0:hi> upon it, which (as we have before observed) was our Saviour's constant practice where he did Eat Bread, but <ns0:hi>he set it apart, and Consecrated it</ns0:hi> for a part of his last Supper. It seemeth very probable, that this is to be understood here in the Word <ns0:hi>Blessed it.</ns0:hi> For altho the Jews, and our Saviour ordinarily used a short <ns0:hi>Prayer</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Thanks<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />giving</ns0:hi> before they did Eat Meat, thereby shewing that they owned God as the giver of those things, and depended upon him for a Blessing upon them, yet we no where Read, that they did so during the same Meal, as often as they put Bread into their Mouths. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> (as we heard before) made a parti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cular mention of our Saviours Blessing the Paschal Supper. The mentioning of ours Saviours Blessing of this Bread, manifestly leadeth us to a new Notion. and Institution, and the repeating of it again, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 27. upon his <ns0:hi>taking the Cup,</ns0:hi> doth yet fur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther Confirm it. That our Saviours <ns0:hi>Blessing</ns0:hi> both the one and the other, signifieth to us not only his giving Thanks to God, and begging of Gods Blessing, as upon ordinary Food, but his Sanctifying the one, and the other to be used as a new Gospel Institution, for the Rememb<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ance of his Death. <ns0:hi>And brake it, and gave it to the Disciples,</ns0:hi> whether (as some say) the Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ster of the Jewish Feasts was wont after begging of a Blessing, thus to break Bread and to give it to all the Guests, I cannot tell, I know no Scripture we have to assure us of it; certain it is our Saviour, <ns0:hi>brake it,</ns0:hi> and did give it to his Disciples; that he gave it into their Mouths, they not touching it with their Hands, or that he gave it into every one of their particular Hands, the Scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture saith not, nor is it very probable, except we will admit, that he changed the posture he was in; for let any Judge how probable it is that one sitting upon his Legs, Leaning, or not Leaning, (the constant posture they used in Eating, whether the Paschal Supper, or any other Meals) keeping his posture, could reach it to eleven Persons in the same posture, to put it into their several Mouths, or give it particularly into every one of their Hands; it is therefore more probable, that he put the Dish, or Vessel in which the Bread was from him; to him that sate next to him, and so it was conveyed from Hand to Hand till all had taken it, after he had first spake as followeth. Those who can think otherwise, must presume that our Lord changed his po<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sture, which I am sure is not to be proved, from any place of ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly Writ. <ns0:hi>And said, Take Eat this is my Body. (Luk</ns0:hi> adds) <ns0:hi>which is given for you. Do this in Remembrance of me. Paul</ns0:hi> puts all together, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 11.24. only for <ns0:hi>given</ns0:hi> he saith <ns0:hi>Broken</ns0:hi> what Contests have been, and yet are betwixt the <ns0:hi>Papists, Lu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tharanes,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Zuinglians</ns0:hi> (since called <ns0:hi>Calvinists</ns0:hi>) about the true sense of those Words. <ns0:hi>This is my Body,</ns0:hi> every one knows. The <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> make the sense this; <ns0:hi>This Bread once Consecrated by the Priest,</ns0:hi> is <ns0:hi>presently turned into the very Body and Blood of Christ, which every Communicant Eateth.</ns0:hi> Hence are their A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dorations to it, their <ns0:hi>Elevations</ns0:hi> of it, their carrying it about in <ns0:hi>So<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lemn Processions</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> &c. The <ns0:hi>Lutherans,</ns0:hi> tho they see the Gross Absurdities of this sense, yet say. <ns0:hi>That the true and real Body and Blood of Christ, in its true substance, is present with the Bread and Wine in the Sacrament, and Eaten by every Communicant.</ns0:hi> Both these opinions agree in this Absurdity, That Christs Body now must be no true humane Body, for we know that all true Humane Bodies are <ns0:hi>subject to our Senses</ns0:hi>; and <ns0:hi>some one place that they cannot at the same time be in another,</ns0:hi> much less in a thou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sand or ten thousand places at the same time. But neither the <ns0:hi>Papist</ns0:hi> nor the <ns0:hi>Lutheranes</ns0:hi> will hear of any Arguments from that Head, but stick to the Letter of our Saviours Words. The <ns0:hi>Zuing<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lians</ns0:hi> say the meaning is. <ns0:hi>This signifieth my Body.</ns0:hi> In the same Sense, as it is said, Christ <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Way,</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>Door,</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>Vine,</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>Shepherd,</ns0:hi> and it is said of the Lamb, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 12.11. <ns0:hi>This is the Lords Passover</ns0:hi>; yet they are far from making it this or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />Ordinance a bare empty Sign, but do acknowledge it a sacred In<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tit<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tion of Christ in the Gospel, in the Observation of which he doth vo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>chsafe his spiritual Presence, so as every true Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />liever worthily receiving, doth <ns0:hi>Really</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Truly</ns0:hi> partake of the <ns0:hi>Bod<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Blood of Christ,</ns0:hi> That is, all Benefits of his Blessed Death, and Passion, which is undoubtedly all intended by our Saviour in these Words; and when he saith, <ns0:hi>Take Eat,</ns0:hi> he means no more, than that true Believers should by the Hand of their Body <ns0:hi>take the Bread,</ns0:hi> and with their bodily Mouths eat it, and at the same time by the Hand, and Mouth of Faith. <ns0:hi>Receive</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>apply,</ns0:hi> all the Benefits of his Blessed Death and Passion, to their Souls; and that they should do this in remembrance of him, that is, (as the Apostle, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 11.26. expounds it) <ns0:hi>shewing forth the Lords Death, till he come.</ns0:hi> It followeth: <ns0:hi>And he took the Cup, and gave Thanks; and gave it to them saying. Drink ye all of it. For this is my Blood of the New Testament, which is shed for many, for the Remission of sins.</ns0:hi> Christ's taking of the Cup, and giving of Thanks, were Actions of the same Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture, with those which he used with a Relation to the Bread, of which I spake before: Let the <ns0:hi>Papists,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Lutherans</ns0:hi> say what they can, here must be two Figures acknowledged in these Words. The <ns0:hi>Cup</ns0:hi> here is put for the <ns0:hi>Wine in the Cup</ns0:hi>; and the meaning of these Words: <ns0:hi>This is my Blood of the New Testament,</ns0:hi> must be: <ns0:hi>This Wine is the sign of the New Covenant.</ns0:hi> Why they should not, as readily acknowledge a Figure in those Words, <ns0:hi>T<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>is is my Body,</ns0:hi> I cannot understand; the Pronoun <ns0:hi>This</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Greek,</ns0:hi> is in the <ns0:hi>Neuter Gender,</ns0:hi> and applicable to the term <ns0:hi>Cup,</ns0:hi> or to the term <ns0:hi>Blood</ns0:hi>; but it is most reasonable to interpret it: <ns0:hi>This Cup,</ns0:hi> That is, the Wine in this Cup, is the <ns0:hi>Blood</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>New Covenant, or Testament</ns0:hi>; That is, the Blood by which the <ns0:hi>New Covenant</ns0:hi> is confirmed, and established. Thus the <ns0:hi>Blood of the Covenant,</ns0:hi> signifieth in several Texts, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 24.8. <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 9.11. 9.20. <ns0:hi>& Heb.</ns0:hi> 10.29. <ns0:hi>Which is shed for many, for the Remission of sins,</ns0:hi> to purchase Remission of sins; and this lets us know, that by <ns0:hi>Many,</ns0:hi> here cannot be understood all individuals, unless we will say, that Christ purchased a Remission of sins for many, who shall never obtain it, which how he could do, if he died in their stead, suffering the Wrath of God due to them for sin, is very hard to understand. <ns0:hi>But I say unto you, that I will not henceforth Drink of the Fruit of the Vine.</ns0:hi> I observed be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore, that <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> puts these Words before the Institution of the Supper, and some think that they properly belong to that place, but I understand no reason for it, <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> both placing it here; nor doth it seem probable, that after these Words, our Saviour should presently Drink of it, in the Institu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of his Supper; some here Object our Saviours drinking after his Resurrection; but besides that, it cannot be proved that he drank any Wine, neither did he otherwise eat, or drink at all, but to shew that he was indeed risen (for he Hungred and Thirsted no more after his Resurrection) Or else by this <ns0:hi>Phrase</ns0:hi> our Saviour only meant, I will no more participate in this Ordinance with you, <ns0:hi>Vntil I drink it New with you in my Fathers Kingdom,</ns0:hi> that is in Heaven. Some will say, <ns0:hi>Shall there then be drinking of Wine in Heaven? Ans.</ns0:hi> No, neither doth the Particle <ns0:hi>Vntil,</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ignifie any such thing: But the Joys and Pleasures of Heaven, are often Metaphorically set out, under the Notion of <ns0:hi>sitting</ns0:hi> down to <ns0:hi>Banquet, Chap.</ns0:hi> 8.11. <ns0:hi>Supping, Rev.</ns0:hi> 3.20. <ns0:hi>Eating and Drinking, Luk.</ns0:hi> 22.30. Our Saviour calls this <ns0:hi>New Wine</ns0:hi> to signi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fie, that he did not by it mean, such Wine as Men drink here: I will not henceforth drink of the Fruit of the Vine, but both you and I in my Fathers Glory, shall be satisfied with Rivers of Plea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sures, which shall be far sweeter, and more Excellent than that, which is but the juyce of the Grape, and the Fruit of the Vine. <ns0:hi>And when they had sung an Hymn, they went out into the Mount of Olives.</ns0:hi> That the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were wont to close their <ns0:hi>Passo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver-Supper</ns0:hi> with singing an <ns0:hi>Hymn</ns0:hi> I do not doubt: Nor that they had some particular <ns0:hi>Psalms,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Hymns,</ns0:hi> which they used at that time to sing: But whether it were any of these, that our Saviour at this time <ns0:hi>Praised God with,</ns0:hi> I cannot tell, much less, whether he designed this <ns0:hi>Praising of God,</ns0:hi> with particular Relation to the <ns0:hi>Paschal-Supper,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>His Supper,</ns0:hi> which he had now instituted, or both. The inquiries after these things, are but insignificant Curiosities, fit for such as have more mind, to look into the skirts of Holy-Writ, than to find out of it, what may be of Profit and Advantage to them. Our Saviour doubtless intended by this to instruct us, That the Ordinance of his Supper, is an <ns0:hi>Eu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />christical Service,</ns0:hi> wherein our Souls are most highly concerned to give Thanks unto God, and as <ns0:hi>Singing,</ns0:hi> is an external Action, which God hath appointed to express the inward Joy and Thankfulness of our Hearts; so it is very proper to be used at that Holy <ns0:hi>Institu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion. They went out to the Mount of Olives.</ns0:hi> Our Lord knew that his time was now come, when he must be actually delivered into the Hands of his Enemies. That he might not therefore cause any disturbance, either to the Master of the Family where<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />in he was, or to the City, tho it was <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ow Midnight, he goeth out of the City (the Gates being either open, (because of the mul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />titude of People) very late; or else easily opened to him) to the <ns0:hi>Mount of Olives.</ns0:hi> A Mountain in the way, betwixt <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Bethany,</ns0:hi> so called, as is thought, from the multitude of <ns0:hi>Olive Trees</ns0:hi> growing upon, and about it. The Evangelist as yet men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioneth nothing of <ns0:hi>Iudas,</ns0:hi> who now was gone to Plot his work, and will anon return to accomplish it. In the mean time let us follow our Saviour, attending to his Discourses and Actions.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:269" />31 Then saith Jesus unto them, <ns0:note place="margin">Joh. 16.32.</ns0:note> All ye shall be offended, because of me this night, for it is writ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ten, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock, shall be scattered abroad.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 But after I am risen again, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 28.16.</ns0:note> I will go before you into Galilee.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 Peter answered and said unto him. Though all men shall be offended because of thee, <ns0:hi>yet</ns0:hi> will I never be offended.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 Jesus saith unto him, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 13.3<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> Verily I say untothee, that this nightbeforethecockcrow thou shalt deny methrice.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 Peter said unto him, Though I should dye with thee, yet will I not deny thee, Likewise also said all the disciples.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.27, 28, 29, 30, 31. only <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 30. he saith: <ns0:hi>This Day, even this Night, before the Cock crow twice,</ns0:hi> Thou shalt deny me thrice. <ns0:hi>Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 22.31, 32, 33.34. hath it not entire, but he hath something of it, with some Addition, thus, <ns0:hi>And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as Wheat. But I have prayed for thee, that thy Faith may not fail, and when thou art converted, strengthen thy Brethren. And he said un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to him, I am ready to go with thee, both into Prison, and to Death. And he said unto him, I tell thee, Peter, that the Cock shall not Crow this Day, before thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.</ns0:hi> Those who read the <ns0:hi>Evangelists,</ns0:hi> must remember that they did not write our Saviours words from his mouth, but from their Memories, and therefore must be allowed to vary in their Expressions, and in Circumstances, giving us only an Account of the substance of Words and Acti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons, as their Memories served them, from whence also it is, that some of them have some Circumstances, not in the others. Our Saviours design here in General, is to inform his Disciples of some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing, which would happen by and by. <ns0:hi>All ye</ns0:hi> (saith he) <ns0:hi>shall be offended, because of me this Night.</ns0:hi> The word <ns0:hi>offended,</ns0:hi> is of a very large Signification in Holy-Writ; here, it seems to sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifie <ns0:hi>disturbed</ns0:hi>; or <ns0:hi>troubled,</ns0:hi> tho if we take it strictly for <ns0:hi>stum<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bling, so as to sin,</ns0:hi> it was true enough, for that happened, (as we shall see anon) which made them to <ns0:hi>forsake Christ and fly,</ns0:hi> which doubtless was their sin. <ns0:hi>For it is written, I will smite the Shepherd and the Sheep of the Flock shall be scattered.</ns0:hi> The words are, <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 13.7. The words there are <ns0:hi>Imperative, smite the Shepherd.</ns0:hi> There are different Opinions, whether that Text is primarily to be understood of <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> or it be only a <ns0:hi>Proverbial Speech,</ns0:hi> which the <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> made use of with another reference, which yet <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> doth apply unto himself. I do more encline to think, that <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> here interpreteth the <ns0:hi>Prophecy,</ns0:hi> to relate <ns0:hi>Primarily</ns0:hi> to himself, for he doth not say, <ns0:hi>As it is said,</ns0:hi> but, <ns0:hi>As it is written,</ns0:hi> yet consider it as a <ns0:hi>Proverbial Speech,</ns0:hi> it is true of others also. But certainly our Saviour designed to up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hold the Spirits of his Disciples, by letting them know, that tho they should see <ns0:hi>the Shepherd smitten,</ns0:hi> that is, <ns0:hi>Himself,</ns0:hi> who is the <ns0:hi>Good Shepherd, Ioh.</ns0:hi> 10.1. and is called by the Apostle, the <ns0:hi>Great Shepherd of the Sheep, Heb.</ns0:hi> 13.20. the <ns0:hi>Chief Shepherd,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 5.4. yet they should not be disturbed, for, 1. <ns0:hi>It was no more than was Prophecied concerning him, Zech.</ns0:hi> 13.7.2. Tho at present they were scattered, yet it should not be long, for he should <ns0:hi>Rise again,</ns0:hi> and then he would <ns0:hi>go before them into Galilee,</ns0:hi> which was fulfilled, as we read, <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 16.7. Upon these words, <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> whom by all the Gospel History, we shall observe to have been of the highest Courage, and forwardest to speak, saith, <ns0:hi>Tho all Men should be offended, yet will I never be offended.</ns0:hi> These doubtless were his present Thoughts, this his sudden Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />solution, here now seem to come in our Saviours Words to <ns0:hi>Pe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter,</ns0:hi> mentioned by <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> only, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 22.31. <ns0:hi>Simon, Simon, Satan hath desired to have you, that he maysift you as Wheat. But I have Prayed that your Faith might not fail, when thou art converted, strengthen thy Brethren.</ns0:hi> You is in the Plural Number, and to be interpreted by <ns0:hi>You all,</ns0:hi> tho our Saviour directeth his Speech only to <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> who first spake, whom he calleth by his own Name; and doubleth it, to signifie his Earnestness in giving him warning. <ns0:hi>To sift you.</ns0:hi> In sifting there are two things. 1. The shaking of the Corn up and down. 2. The Separation of the Grain, from the Dust, or its Seeds mixt with it: <ns0:hi>Satan</ns0:hi> hath desired, or hath obtained leave of my Father, to trouble you all, shaking your Faith this and that way. But I have Prayed, that altho the work<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ings of your Faith be suspended, and the Habit of your Faith be shaken, yet it may not utterly fail, but the Seeds of God may abide in you: You shall not wholly fall away, but be renewed again by Repentance, and <ns0:hi>when thou art converted,</ns0:hi> when thou hast fallen, and shalt have a sight of thy Error, and be humbled for it, indeavour to strengthen thy Brethrens Faith: We may observe from hence. 1. <ns0:hi>That Temptations are siftings.</ns0:hi> God sifts us to purge away our Dross. Satan sifts us, if it were possi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble to take away our Wheat. 2. <ns0:hi>That the Devil is the great Tempter.</ns0:hi> Others may hold, and move the Sieve, but he is the Master of the Work. 3. <ns0:hi>That he hath a continual desire to be sif<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ting in God's Flower.</ns0:hi> 4. <ns0:hi>That he hath a Chain upon him,</ns0:hi> he must ask Gods leave to trouble his People. 5. <ns0:hi>That God often giveth him leave, but through Christs pleadings, he shall not Conquer.</ns0:hi> He may sift and trouble a Believer, but the Believers Faith shall not fail. 6. <ns0:hi>That in the hour of Temptation, we stand in Christs strength,</ns0:hi> by the Vertue of his Intercession. 7. <ns0:hi>That lapsed Chri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stians, when the Lord hath restored them, ought to indeavour to strengthen and establish others.</ns0:hi> Jesus saith to <ns0:hi>Peter, Veril<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> I say unto thee, that this Night before the Cock crow thou shalt deny me thrice. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Thou shalt deny that thou knowest me. Mark</ns0:hi> saith, before the <ns0:hi>Cock crow twice:</ns0:hi> And so inter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />preteth <ns0:hi>Matthew,</ns0:hi> for he denied Christ but once, before the Cock did crow once. How little do we know our selves, that cannot tell what our Hearts will be, three or four hours? <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> was too confident of the contrary, and replyeth again, upon our Saviour telling him: That if all should deny him, he would not. So also, they all said, but what happened we shall hear more by and by.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:269" />36 Then came Jesus with them, unto a place called Gethsemane, and saith unto the disciples, Sit ye here, while I go and pray yonder.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> leaveth out <ns0:hi>Yonder, Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.32. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 22.39. <ns0:hi>He came out, and w<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>nt as he was wont, to the Mount of Olives, and his Disciples followed him. And when he was at the place, he said unto them: Pray that you enter not into Temptation. And he was withdrawn from them a stones cast, and kneeled down and Prayed.</ns0:hi> Whether this <ns0:hi>Gethsemane,</ns0:hi> were the name of a Gar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />den, or of a <ns0:hi>Village,</ns0:hi> wherein was a Garden, is not much Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terial for us to know: In <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> they say, they had no Gar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dens, but their Gardens were without the Gates; certain it is, it was on the other side of the Brook <ns0:hi>Cedron, Ioh.</ns0:hi> 18.1. and either in, or at the Foot of the Mount of <ns0:hi>Olives.</ns0:hi> Thither Christ went with his Disciples: That is, eleven of them, we shall hear of the twelfth by and by, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, that he bad his Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciples <ns0:hi>Pray, that they might not enter into Temp<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ation:</ns0:hi> These Words <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> have, after Christ's first return to them: They say, he now said only, <ns0:hi>Sit you here, while I go and Pray yonder.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 And he took with him Peter, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 4.21.</ns0:note> the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">John 12.27.</ns0:note> and very heavy.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 Then saith he unto them, My soul is exceed<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing sorrowful unto death, tarry ye here, and watch with me.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> names the three Disciples, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 33, 34. <ns0:hi>And he taketh with him Peter and Iames, and Iohn, and began to be sore amazed, and to be very heavy. And saith unto them, my Soul is exceeding sorrowful unto Death: Tarry ye here and Watch.</ns0:hi> The three <ns0:hi>Witnesses</ns0:hi> of his <ns0:hi>Transfiguration, Ch.</ns0:hi> 17.1. He takes also to be <ns0:hi>Witness</ns0:hi> of his <ns0:hi>Agony, He began to be Sorrowful,</ns0:hi> and very <ns0:hi>Heavy.</ns0:hi> The words in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> are ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pressive of the greatest Sorrow imaginable, which he further ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />presseth, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 38. Saying, <ns0:hi>My Soul is exceeding sorrowful unto Death.</ns0:hi> This was not wholly, upon the Sense of his approaching Death, for he <ns0:hi>laid down his Life, no Man took it from him.</ns0:hi> Nor yet, to consider how his Disciples would be left; but in the Sense he had, of the Wrath of God due to Man for sin, which he now felt, bearing our sins. So as this was a part, and a great part of his suffering, as appears by his following earnest Prayers, for the passing away of that Cup, his <ns0:hi>Sweating</ns0:hi> as it were <ns0:hi>drops of Blood, Luk.</ns0:hi> 22.44. The Angels coming and Ministring unto him, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 22.43. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, he was in an <ns0:hi>Agony,</ns0:hi> which sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifieth a great inward Conflict.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 And he went a little further, and fell on his face <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Heb. 5.7.</ns0:note> and prayed, saying, O my Father if it be possible, let this cup pass from me, nevertheless not as I will, but as thou <ns0:hi>wilt.</ns0:hi>
                  <ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>He went forward a little, and fell on the Ground, and Prayed, that if it were possible, the hour might pass from him. And he said, Abba Father! All things are possible unto thee, take away this Cup from me: Nevertheless, not what I will, but what thou wilt, Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.35, 36. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>He was withdrawn from them about a stones Cast, and kneeled down, and Prayed, Saying, Father if thou be willing, remove this Cup from me: Nevertheless, not my Will, but thine be done.</ns0:hi> Here are three distinct Forms of Words, but all agreeing in one, and the same Sense. <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>He went a little further and fell on his Face, and Prayed.</ns0:hi> He at his first Mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion carried but three with him: <ns0:hi>Peter, Iames,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> now he leaves them, but not far, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, about a <ns0:hi>stones Cast.</ns0:hi> Fervent Prayer loves Privacy, and Christ by this teacheth us, that <ns0:hi>secret Prayer</ns0:hi> is our Duty, <ns0:hi>He fell on his Face, Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>He kneeled,</ns0:hi> he possibly at first <ns0:hi>Kneeled,</ns0:hi> then <ns0:hi>fell on his Face:</ns0:hi> We read in Scripture of <ns0:hi>Sitting, Standing, Kneeling,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stration</ns0:hi> used in <ns0:hi>Prayer,</ns0:hi> the first and last rarely<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Standing</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Kneeling,</ns0:hi> were the most ordinary Postures. <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> prayed sit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ting in his House, 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 7.18. <ns0:hi>Abraham fell on his Face, Gen.</ns0:hi> 17.17. So did <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Aaron, Numb.</ns0:hi> 16.22.45. <ns0:hi>Prostra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion</ns0:hi> was ordinarily use<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> in great Passions, hardly otherwise in Prayer. <ns0:hi>Saying, O my Father if it be possible, let this Cup pass from me: Nevertheless, not as I Will, but as thou wilt. Mark</ns0:hi> first tells us the Sum of his Prayer, then saith, he said <ns0:hi>Abba Father! All things are possible unto thee: Take away this Cup from me: Nevertheless, not what I Will, but what thou wilt. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, he said, <ns0:hi>If thou be willing, remove this Cup from me: Nevertheless, not my Will, but thine be done. Luke's, If thou be willing,</ns0:hi> expounds <ns0:hi>Matthew's if it be possible.</ns0:hi> A thing in it self may be possible, which considered in its Circumstances is not so, thus (as it is,) <ns0:hi>Mark, All things are to God possible:</ns0:hi> But yet it is not possible for God to al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter any thing which he hath decreed, or said shall come to pass<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> because God is not as Man: <ns0:hi>One that can Lye,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Repent.</ns0:hi> But it will be Objected. <ns0:hi>Did not Christ know, that it was not possi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble?</ns0:hi> Did not he himself, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 54. say. <ns0:hi>Thus it must be?</ns0:hi> I an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swer, It is one thing what he knew, <ns0:hi>as he was God,</ns0:hi> and of Coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cel with the Father; and another thing what he Prayed for, <ns0:hi>a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> Man:</ns0:hi> Besides, our Saviours saying, <ns0:hi>If it be possible,</ns0:hi> doth not suppose that he knew it was possible: It signifieth no more than this. <ns0:hi>Father,</ns0:hi> my Humane Nature hath an Aversion from this heavy stroke, so as if it were possible, it craves of thee a Discharge from this Curse: <ns0:hi>Nevertheless, not my Will, but thine be done.</ns0:hi> The first Clause, is but the Expression of the natural (but not sinful) infirmity of his Flesh: The latter a <ns0:hi>perfect Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />signation,</ns0:hi> of his Will to God. In the first, he tells his Father, what his natural Flesh would crave, if it might consist with the Will of God. In the second, he begs that whatsoever his Flesh craved, yet the Will of God might be done. And herein he sets us a perfect Pattern for our Prayers, for deliverance from Temporal Evils, viz. With a Submission to the Will of God. By this, our Saviour doth not declare himself ignorant, or incer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain of the Divine Will. Only as, tho the Person that dyed was <ns0:hi>God-man,</ns0:hi> yet the Humane Nature only dyed: So, tho the Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son that prayed was <ns0:hi>God-man,</ns0:hi> yet he only prayed, as he was Man.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 And he cometh unto the disciples, and find<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth them asleep, and saith unto Peter, What, could ye not watch with me one hour?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 Watch, and pray, that ye enter not into temptati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on: The spirit indeed <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> willing, but theflesh <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> weak.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.37, 38. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath nothing of our Saviour's going the second, or third time; but hath some other passages, which we shall consider by and by, and telleth us but once, of his finding the <ns0:hi>Disciples asleep,</ns0:hi> which we shall also take notice of, in their Order. Whether Christ came this first time, only to <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iames,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> whom he had left nearer to him, or to the other eight, left at a further distance, I cannot determine, but think the first most probable: He saith unto <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> and so to <ns0:hi>Iames and Iohn: What could ye not Watch with me one Hour?</ns0:hi> You <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> that even now wert so resolute for me, and you <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> that told me, <ns0:hi>You could Drink of the Cup whereof I Drank, and be baptized with the Baptism I should be baptized with, what?</ns0:hi> Do you faint the first time? <ns0:hi>Watch and Pray, that you enter not into Tempta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion.</ns0:hi> Here he calls them to a greater <ns0:hi>Watching,</ns0:hi> spiritual Watch<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, in Opposition to <ns0:hi>Security,</ns0:hi> that they might not fall under their Temptations. By watching, he directeth them to the use of such means, as were within their Power to use; by adding <ns0:hi>Pray,</ns0:hi> he lets them know, that it was not in their Power, to stand with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out Gods help and Assistance, which must be obtained by Prayer, and upon their Praying, should not be denied them. <ns0:hi>The Spirit indeed is Willing, but the Flesh is Weak.</ns0:hi> The Spirit sanctified by Divine Grace, is resolved with Constancy to perform its Duty; but the Flesh, the sensitive part, is apt to Faint and fall away, when terrible Temptations assault us: Therefore you should earnestly pray for super-natural strength, and be Vigilant, lest you be surprized and overcome by them. The words also, may have an immediate Respect to their being overtaken with sleep in this hour of Christ's Summons; tho they resolved Affectionately to attend him, and cleave to him.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 He went away again the second time, and prayed, saying, O my Father if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="43">43 And he came, and found them asleep again, for their eyes were heavy.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.39. <ns0:hi>And again he went away and Prayed, saying the same Words. And when he returned he found them asleep again (for their Eyes were heavy) neither wist they what to Answer him, saying the same Words.</ns0:hi> How our Translation came to translate this so I cannot tell, in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> it is <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, which must be Translated, The same <ns0:hi>Word,</ns0:hi> or the <ns0:hi>same Speech,</ns0:hi> not <ns0:hi>Words</ns0:hi> (if that were the Evangelists Sense.) But that it is not, for as it is plain, our Saviour used more than <ns0:hi>one Word.</ns0:hi> So it is as plain, it was not the same <ns0:hi>Speech,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Form</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Words,</ns0:hi> for we have met with four different Forms already, Our Lord prayed but thrice, so as he could not say the <ns0:hi>same Speech.</ns0:hi> But <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> here signifies Matter.—Speaking the same Matter, or to the same Sense, and thus we translate it, <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 1.45. <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 2.2. and in a multitude of other Texts, in Cor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />respondence with the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. He comes to them a second time, and findeth them asleep. So quickly did they find the Truth of what he had but now taught them. <ns0:hi>That the Spirit is willing, but the Flesh is Weak,</ns0:hi> for there is no doubt but they did what they could to keep themselves awake.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="44">44 And he left them, and went away again, and prayed the third time, saying, the same words.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="45">45 Then cometh he to his disciples, and saith, Sleep on now, and take your rest, behold the hour is at hand, and the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="46">46 Rise, let us be going, Behold he is at hand, that doth betray me.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith nothing of this <ns0:hi>third Praying,</ns0:hi> but saith, <ns0:hi>And he cometh the third time, and saith unto them, sleep on now, and take your rest, the Hour is come, Behold the Son of Man is betrayed into the Hands of Sinners, Rise, let us go, lo he that betrayeth me is at Hand</ns0:hi>; what the meaning of <ns0:hi>saying the same Words</ns0:hi> is, we heard before, praying to the same sense, or saying the <ns0:hi>same thing,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>matter,</ns0:hi> tho using other Words, as it is plain he did, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 22.43. tells us, <ns0:hi>There appeared an Angel to him strengthening him.</ns0:hi> This is not the first time we read of <ns0:hi>Angels</ns0:hi> appearing and Ministring to Christ. They did so, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 4.11. after his Conflict with the Devil, in the Wilderness. Now an <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> appeared to him in the Hour of <ns0:hi>Temptation.</ns0:hi> Then he had <ns0:hi>without, troubles.</ns0:hi> But now he hath <ns0:hi>within, Fears,</ns0:hi> being in a great Agony. Thus it is said, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 12.27. that he being in a conflict, and praying, <ns0:hi>Father save me from this Hour; but for this cause I came unto this Hour. Father! Glorify thy Name. A Voice was heard,</ns0:hi> saying, <ns0:hi>I have both Glorifyed it, and will glorify it again.</ns0:hi> There the Answer was Testifyed by a <ns0:hi>Voice</ns0:hi> from <ns0:hi>Heaven,</ns0:hi> Here, it is by an <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> (so God, <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 9.21. let <ns0:hi>Daniel</ns0:hi> know his Prayer was heard) <ns0:hi>Hannah</ns0:hi> knew another way by <ns0:hi>the Peace of her Spirit</ns0:hi> after Prayer—<ns0:hi>her Countenance was no more sad.</ns0:hi> How the Angel did strengthen him we are not told. Let no Man think that he who was the Son of God needed an <ns0:hi>Angel to strengthen him</ns0:hi>: he was not now ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />erting his Divine Verture, but by his suffering shewing that he was truly Man, and as to that nature, made lower than the Angels. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> addeth, <ns0:hi>And being in an Agony he prayed more earnestly, and his Sweat was as it were great drops of Blood, falling down to the Ground, v.</ns0:hi> 44. These Words are Expre<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sive of the great Conflict of our Saviours Spirit, which was such as thrust out <ns0:hi>Sweat</ns0:hi> like great <ns0:hi>drops</ns0:hi> of Blood, whether they were very Blood, or Sweat with some mixture or Tincture of Blood, is very hard to determine, nor of any Consequence for us to know, it is no unusual thing for Bodies to breath out Sweat in ordinary Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />flicts of Spirit, this was much more than ordinary. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, that <ns0:hi>when he rose up from Prayer, and was come to his Disci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ples, he found them Sleeping, for Sorrow. And said unto them, why Sleep you? Rise and Pray lest ye enter into Temptation.</ns0:hi> All three Evangelists agree, that Christ coming the <ns0:hi>third time found them Sleeping, Luke</ns0:hi> gives one Reason of it <ns0:hi>for Sorrow.</ns0:hi> Their <ns0:hi>sorrow</ns0:hi> added to their <ns0:hi>Watching,</ns0:hi> may be some excuse for their sleeping, tho otherwise it was a time which called for more Waking. The <ns0:hi>Evangelists</ns0:hi> do not so well agree in what Christ said to his D<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sciples. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Rise up and pray lest you en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter into Temptation. Matthew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> say, he said, <ns0:hi>Sleep on now and take your Rest,</ns0:hi> &c. he might say both. Nor can we determine whether he spake those Words <ns0:hi>seriously,</ns0:hi> as willing that they should t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ke their Rest, for they could be no further useful to him, whose time was now come, he was betrayed, and the Traytor was at Hand: Or, with some Reflection upon them, for their Drowsiness, which the Words going before, <ns0:hi>what could you not Watch with me one Hour</ns0:hi>? seem to hint us.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="47">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:270" />47 And while he yet spake, lo Judas one of the twelve came, and with him a great multitude, with swords and staves, from the chief priests, and elders of the people.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.43. adding also the <ns0:hi>Scribes. Luke</ns0:hi> saith there was a <ns0:hi>Multitude,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iudas went before them</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> adding, that he <ns0:hi>drew near to Iesus to kiss him, Luke</ns0:hi> 22.47, If any ask, How <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> knew where <ns0:hi>Iesus</ns0:hi> was at that time of the Night, or rather so early in the Morning. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> satisfieth us, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 18.2. <ns0:hi>And</ns0:hi> Judas <ns0:hi>also which betray'd him, knew the place, for Iesus oft times resorted thither with his Disciples.</ns0:hi> And then goeth on Judas <ns0:hi>then having received a Band of Men, and Officers, from the Chief Priests and Pharisees cometh thither, with Lantherns, and Torches, and Weapons.</ns0:hi> Those skilled in the Jewish Learning tell us, that the ordinary Guard of the Temple belonged to the <ns0:hi>Priests,</ns0:hi> and such Officers as they imploy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed; but upo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> their great Festivals, the <ns0:hi>Roman Governour</ns0:hi> add<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed a <ns0:hi>Band of his Souldiers,</ns0:hi> who yet were under the command of the <ns0:hi>Priests.</ns0:hi> It is thought these Officers, Souldiers and others came with a Warrant to apprehend our Saviour from the <ns0:hi>Iewish Sanhedrim</ns0:hi> or highest Court, which was made up of <ns0:hi>Chief Priests, Scribes, and Pharisees, and the Elders of the People,</ns0:hi> they had <ns0:hi>Torches</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Lentherns,</ns0:hi> because it was yet dark, before the Day was broke. Swords and Staves to be ready against any Opposition. <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Traytor</ns0:hi> comes before as their Lea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="48">48 Now he that betrayed him, gave them a sign saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he, hold him fast.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="49">49 And forthwith he came to Jesus, and said, Hail master, and kissed him.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark, Ch.</ns0:hi> 14. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 44, 45. differs not, only instead of <ns0:hi>Hold him fast,</ns0:hi> he hath, <ns0:hi>Lead him away safely,</ns0:hi> and instead of <ns0:hi>Hail Master</ns0:hi>! he saith, <ns0:hi>Master, Master.</ns0:hi> There is in these Words nothing difficult or doubtful, <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> had given them a sign how to know Christ, that was his Kissing of him, being come where he was he steps to our Saviour and kissed him, by which he let them know, that he was the Person against whom their Warrant was.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="50">50 And Jesus saith unto him, Friend, where<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore art thou come? Then came they, and laid hands on Jesus, and took him.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith nothing of what Christ said to him, <ns0:hi>Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 22.48. adds, that Christ said to him, <ns0:hi>Iudas, betrayest thou the Son of Man with a Kiss</ns0:hi>? Whether <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> used this Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pellation of <ns0:hi>Friend</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Iudas,</ns0:hi> to mind him what he formerly had been, and still ought to have been, or as a Common Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pellation, (as we oft use it) is not much Material. A Kiss is the Symbol of Friendship, and Kindness, and therefore very im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />poperly used by a <ns0:hi>Traytor</ns0:hi> and professed Enemy (yet so used by <ns0:hi>Ioab</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Amasa,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 20.9.) That makes our Saviour ask him, if he were not ashamed to betray the Son of Man by a Kiss. <ns0:hi>Iu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />das,</ns0:hi> by calling him <ns0:hi>Master, Master,</ns0:hi> acknowledged he had been once his disciple. By his Kiss, he pretended Friendship to him, yet <ns0:hi>betrayed</ns0:hi> him. O the depth of desperate Wickedness, which is in the Heart of Man! especially such as Apostatize from a for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mer <ns0:hi>Profession,</ns0:hi> they are commonly the worst and falsest Ene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mies of Christ, and his Gospel.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
