               <ns0:p n="51">51 And behold one of them which were with Jesus stretched out his hand, and drew his sword, and stroke a servant of the high priests, and smote off his ear.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="52">52 Then said Jesus unto him, Put up again thy sword into his place, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 9.6. Rev. 13.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> for all they that take the sword shall perish with the sword.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="53">53 Thinkest thou that I cannot now pray to my fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, and he shall presently give me more then twelve legions of Angels?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="54">54 But how then shall the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Is<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 53.7. & Luke 2.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 46.</ns0:note> scriptures be fulfilled that thus it must be?<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> relates this History shortly, but <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> much more, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.47. he saith no more than this. <ns0:hi>And one of them that stood by, drew a Sword, and smote a Servant of the High Priest, and cut off his Ear. Luke</ns0:hi> also relates something of it in, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 22.50.51. And one of them smote a Servant of the High <ns0:hi>Priest,</ns0:hi> and cut off his <ns0:hi>Right Ear. And Iesus answered and said. Suffer ye thus far, and he touched his Ear and healed it. Iohn</ns0:hi> relates the same passage with some more particulars, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 18.10. <ns0:hi>Then Simon Peter having a Sword drew it, and smote the High Priests Servant, and cut off his Right Ear.</ns0:hi> The Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vants Name was <ns0:hi>Malchus. Then said Iesus unto</ns0:hi> Peter, <ns0:hi>Put up thy Sword into the Sheath. The Cup which my Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther hath given me to Drink, shall I not Drink it</ns0:hi>? If a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny ask, how Christ and his Disciples came to have a Sword, he may be satisfyed that they had two, from <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 22. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 35, 36, 37, 38. (which Verses being in none of the other Evangelists, I have left, to be spoken to in their order) The Disciples seeing the Officers (as was said <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 50.) laying Hands on Christ, as <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>knowing what would follow. One of them,</ns0:hi> (St. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> tells us it was <ns0:hi>Peter) drew a Sword,</ns0:hi> and smote off the <ns0:hi>Right Ear</ns0:hi> of one of the <ns0:hi>High Priests</ns0:hi> Servants. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> tells us his Name was <ns0:hi>Malchus.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour reproveth <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> command<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing him to <ns0:hi>put up the Sword again into its Sheath,</ns0:hi> and telling him, <ns0:hi>That he who taketh the Sword, should Perish with the Sword.</ns0:hi> It is to be understood of private Persons, taking up the Sword to destroy their Lawful <ns0:hi>Magistrates,</ns0:hi> and this Les<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son it teacheth all Christians. Men must have the Sword given orderly into their Hands, before they may use it, and that no <ns0:hi>private Person</ns0:hi> can have against the <ns0:hi>Supream Magistrate.</ns0:hi> 2. 2. Secondly, (saith our Saviour) I needed not thy help to de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fend me, If I were to make any defence, I could pray to my <ns0:hi>Father,</ns0:hi> and he should give me more then twelve Legions of <ns0:hi>Angels,</ns0:hi> there is therefore no need of thy drawing a Sword in my defence. 3. <ns0:hi>The Scripture</ns0:hi> (saith he) <ns0:hi>must be fulfilled,</ns0:hi> it was Prophesied of me that I should be thus used, and those <ns0:hi>Prophesies</ns0:hi> must <ns0:hi>be fulfilled.</ns0:hi> Having reproved <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> and silenced his Pas<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> tells us, he begged leave so far as to <ns0:hi>touch his Ear,</ns0:hi> and he <ns0:hi>healed it,</ns0:hi> thus doing good to those that hated him, and working a Miracle in the sight of them, which (had not their Hearts been hardened) might have convinced them, both of his <ns0:hi>Inno<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cency,</ns0:hi> and his <ns0:hi>Divine Power,</ns0:hi> but they take no notice of his kind<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness. Now he applyeth himself to the Multitude of his Enemies.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="55">55 In that same hour said Jesus to the multitudes, Are ye come out as against a thief with swords and staves, for to take me? I sate daily with you teaching in the Temple, and ye laid no hold on me.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 But all this was done, that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">La<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 4 <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled, Then all the disciples forsook him, and fled.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 48, 49, 50. <ns0:hi>Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 22. 52, 53. hath it thus. <ns0:hi>Then Iesus said unto the Chief Priests, and the Captains of the Temple, and the Elders which were come to him, Be ye come out as against a Thief, with Swords, and Staves? when I was daily with you in the Temple, you stretched forth no Ha<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ds against me. But this is your Hour, and the Power of darknest.</ns0:hi> What our <ns0:hi>Evangelist</ns0:hi> reports as spoken to the Rabble, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> reports as spoken to the <ns0:hi>Chief Priests,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Captains</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Temple</ns0:hi> (that is, of the Souldiers, who at that time were the <ns0:hi>Guard of the Temple</ns0:hi>) some of which it should seem, came along with the Rabble, to whom our Saviour directeth his Speech. <ns0:hi>I sate daily with you Teaching in the Temple.</ns0:hi> I observed before that it was their usual manner, for those that Taught in the Temple to <ns0:hi>Sit</ns0:hi> while they Taught, to Testify their Authority, Christ when he came up to the <ns0:hi>Passo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver,</ns0:hi> was wont to Teach in the <ns0:hi>Temple, and you laid no hold on me.</ns0:hi> I did not hide my self, nor go about to raise a party to defend my self, but quietly taught in the Temple, if I had been guilty of any Crime you might easily have taken me, why are you now come out against me, as against a Thief, upon whom you had need to raise the Country? why come you against me with Swords, and Staves? as if you thought I would make some Resistance to defend my self? you never saw any such thing in me, as should give you a jealousie of such a thing? <ns0:hi>But all this was done that the Scriptures of the Prophets might be fulfilled.</ns0:hi> The many Scriptures, which spake concerning the sufferings of Christ. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> addeth, <ns0:hi>But this is your Hour, and the Power of darkness,</ns0:hi> that is, this is that which God hath de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />termined. Wicked Men and Persecutors of Christ, and his Go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />spel, have their <ns0:hi>Hour.</ns0:hi> There is a time which God in his wise Counsels hath set, and determined, when for the Tryal of his Peoples <ns0:hi>Faith,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Patience,</ns0:hi> he suffers the Devil by vile and wicked Men, who are his Instruments, to imprison and otherwise vex, and molest his People. That such a time is <ns0:hi>their Hour,</ns0:hi> and what they do is by the Permission and according to the Counsel of God, and <ns0:hi>but an Hour,</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>determined,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>short time,</ns0:hi> are great Arguments for to persuade us to the Exercise of <ns0:hi>Faith,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Patience. And the Power of darkness.</ns0:hi> A time when the <ns0:hi>Prince of darkness</ns0:hi> is putting forth his Power: or the <ns0:hi>Power of darkness,</ns0:hi> that is, a time of <ns0:hi>exceeding great</ns0:hi> darkness, of Affliction to me, and my Disciples. Wicked Mens Hour is always to Christs Disciples <ns0:hi>the Power of Darkness. And all his Disciples forsook him and fled.</ns0:hi> Probably all of them fled at first, tho <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> and another came back again: Or, <ns0:hi>All</ns0:hi> here signifieth the most of them. We ne<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver know our Hearts upon the prospect of great Tryals, until we come to grapple with them, and to be ingaged in them. These Disciples had all said, They would not forsake him, when it comes to the push, not one of them stands by him. But altho they shrunk at first, not without the Providence of God per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mitting them thus to fail in their Duty, then Governing their failers to his own Glory: yet they again returned to their Duty, after Christs Resurrection, owned Christ, preached his Gospel, and at last drank off the Cup, which he Drank of first, and were Baptized with the Baptisme, wherewith he was Baptized. All must not not be Condemned for Flight in a time of Persecution. We must observe whether they Apostatize from their Profession, or whether they do not return again, before we pass a Judgment against them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="57">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:270" />57 And they that had laid hold on Jesus, led <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> away to Caiphas the high priest, where the scribes, and the elders were assembled.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark, Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.53. saith. <ns0:hi>They led Iesus away to the High Priest, and with him were assembled all the Chief Priests, and the Elders, and the Scribes. Luke</ns0:hi> saith no more but <ns0:hi>Then they took him, and led him, and brought him into the High Priests House, Ch.</ns0:hi> 22.54. John <ns0:hi>saith, Then the Band, and the Captain, and the Officers of the Iews, took Iesus, and Bound him. And led him away to</ns0:hi> Annas <ns0:hi>first, for he was Father-in-Law to</ns0:hi> Caiphas, <ns0:hi>who was the High Priest that same Year. Ioh.</ns0:hi> 18.12, 13. All things were now out of order in the Jewish Church. Regularly, their <ns0:hi>High Priests</ns0:hi> were to be such as derived from the Eldest Son of <ns0:hi>Aaron,</ns0:hi> and were to hold in their place for Life, but they were now chosen <ns0:hi>Annually,</ns0:hi> and their Conquerours ruled the choice as they pleased. Yet some think, that in this the Jews kept something of their Ancient form, and the <ns0:hi>High Priest</ns0:hi> was chosen Regularly of the House of <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi> and for <ns0:hi>Life,</ns0:hi> but the <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> when they listed turned him out, and sold the Place to another, and such a one was <ns0:hi>Caiphas,</ns0:hi> who was at that time <ns0:hi>High Priest,</ns0:hi> Son-in-Law to <ns0:hi>Annas</ns0:hi>; their carrying of Christ first to <ns0:hi>Annas</ns0:hi> his House, was no more than to stay there a while till <ns0:hi>Caiphas,</ns0:hi> and the Council which was appointed to meet that Morning at the House of <ns0:hi>Caiphas</ns0:hi> could assemble.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="58">58 But Peter followed him afar off unto the high priests palace, and went in, and sate with the servants to see the end.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> adds, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.54. and <ns0:hi>warmed himself at the Fire. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 22.54, 55. <ns0:hi>Then took they him, and led him, and brought him to the High Priests House, and</ns0:hi> Peter <ns0:hi>followed afar off, and when they had Kindled a Fire in the midst of the Hall, and were set down together,</ns0:hi> Peter <ns0:hi>sate down amongst them. Iohn</ns0:hi> gives us a more particular account, how <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> came into the Hall, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 18, 15. <ns0:hi>And</ns0:hi> Simon Peter <ns0:hi>followed Iesus, so did a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nother Disciple, that Disciple was known unto the High Priest, and went in with Iesus into the Palace of the High Priest. But</ns0:hi> Peter <ns0:hi>stood at the Door without. Then went out that other Disciple, which was known unto the High Priest, and spake un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to her that kept the Door, and brought in</ns0:hi> Peter. Some think that this other Disciple was <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> himself, but it is not probable that <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>High Priest</ns0:hi> should be so well acquainted, it is more probably judged, That it was none of the Twelve, but one who favoured Christ more secretly, some Citizen of <ns0:hi>Ieru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />salem</ns0:hi> whom the <ns0:hi>High Priest</ns0:hi> favoured, or at least knew by Face, and had some respect for, and therefore he was admitted in, and he helped <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> in, who being come in, and a Fire kindled in the Hall, the rest of the Company sate down and<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> warmed themselves by the Fire, <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> also sate down amongst them, being desi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rous to see the end.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="59">59 Now the chief priests, and elders, and all the council sought false witnesses against Jesus to put him to death.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="60">60 But found none, yea, tho many false witnesses came, yet they found none. At the last came two false witnesses.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> Expounds this latter Verse, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 56. <ns0:hi>For ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny bare false Witness against him, but their Witness agreed not together.</ns0:hi> It is plain that they had taken up a Resolution to destroy Christ one way, or another, but they will make a Shew of Justice, in the Execution of their Malice. The Council be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing sate, it is not to be thought that they had then Leisure to send about for Witnesses, but out of their Malice, they screwed, and fifted such Witnesses as were brought to see if they could get of them upon their Oaths, to affirm any thing against them, which by their Law was Capital. <ns0:hi>Many false Witnesses came, yet they found none.</ns0:hi> That is, no two agreeing in the same Story, as the Law required, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 19.15. for a single Testimo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny was none. <ns0:hi>Vox unius est Vox nullius.</ns0:hi> A single Witness, is no Witness. Or none that could testify any thing of a <ns0:hi>Capital Nature,</ns0:hi> many came and Witnessed <ns0:hi>Trivial things,</ns0:hi> but none Witnessed any thing which touched his Life, till at last came <ns0:hi>two false Witnesses.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="61">61 And said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 27.40,</ns0:note> This <ns0:hi>fellow</ns0:hi> said, I am able to destroy the temple of God, and to build it in three days.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.57, 58, 59. <ns0:hi>And there arose certain, and bare false Witness against him, saying, We heard him say, I will destroy this Temple, that is made with Hands, and with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />in three Days I will build another made without Hands. But neither so did their Witness agree together.</ns0:hi> These are called by the Evangelists, <ns0:hi>false Witnesses</ns0:hi>; our Saviour said, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 2.19. <ns0:hi>Destroy ye this Temple, and in three Days I will raise it up,</ns0:hi> Speaking of his Body, as <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> tells us there. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 21. he did not say, <ns0:hi>I will destroy this Temple, made with Hands, and within three Days I will Build another, made without Hands.</ns0:hi> But <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, These Witnesses could not agree in their Tale, or their Testimony, tho agreeing was not sufficient to make him guilty of a Capital Crime. The <ns0:hi>High Priest</ns0:hi> must use some other Arts.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="62">62 And the high priest, arose, and said unto him, Answerest thou nothing? what <ns0:hi>is it which</ns0:hi> these wit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness against thee.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="63">63 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 53.7. Cha. 22.12.</ns0:note> Jesus held his peace, And the high priest answered, and said unto him, I adjure thee by the living God, that thou tells us, whether thou be the Christ the Son of God.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> speaks to the same purpose, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.60, 61. The <ns0:hi>High Priest,</ns0:hi> expected a long defence, and so to have had mat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter of Accusation against him out of his own Mouth. Christ disappointeth him, saying nothing at all, either out of <ns0:hi>Modesty,</ns0:hi> or not thinking what they said of any Moment, or worthy of any reply, or perhaps seeing that they could not agree in their Tale, so as what they said was of no force against him. The <ns0:hi>High Priest</ns0:hi> therefore comes at last to examine him, <ns0:hi>Ex of<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ficio. Mark</ns0:hi> saith <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.61. <ns0:hi>Again the High Priest asked him, and said unto him, Art thou the Christ the Son of the Blessed. Luke</ns0:hi> to give us the Story of <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> from his fir<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t coming into the <ns0:hi>High Priests</ns0:hi> Hall to his going out, entire, interrupteth himself a little in his Relation of their dealings with Christ, and then relates some Indignities offered him, which the other Evangelists do not mention. Which seem to have been offered him, while the Souldiers and the Rabble had been before he appeared in the Council, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 22.63, 64, 65, 66, 67. <ns0:hi>And the Men that held Iesus mocked him, and Smote him, and when they had Blindfolded him, they stroke him on the Face, and asked him, saying, Prophesie who is it, that smote thee? And many other things, Blasphemously they spake against him. And as soon as it was Day, the Elders of the Peop<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>e, and the Chief Priests, and the Scribes came together, and led him into their Council.</ns0:hi> Then he mentioneth nothing of what the Witnesses said, possibly because it was nothing of Moment, nothing upon which they proceeded against our Saviour <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>or his Life, but goes on—Saying, <ns0:hi>art thou the Christ, tell us. Mat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thew</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>art thou the Christ the Son of the Living God. Mark,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Son of the B<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>essed.</ns0:hi> It is plain both from this Text, and from <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.49. that the Jews did expect a <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> who should be the Son of the <ns0:hi>Ever-living</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Blessed God,</ns0:hi> but whe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther they understood that he should be the <ns0:hi>Son of God by Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Eternal Generation,</ns0:hi> or only by a more <ns0:hi>special Adop<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion,</ns0:hi> than the whole <ns0:hi>Iewish Nation</ns0:hi> was (to whom the Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stle saith belonged the <ns0:hi>Adoption</ns0:hi>) I cannot say. <ns0:hi>I adjure thee to tell us,</ns0:hi> that is, as some say, I charge thee upon thy Oath to tell me (but it doth not appear that they had given any such <ns0:hi>Oath</ns0:hi> to him, the <ns0:hi>Guilty</ns0:hi> Person was not wont to be forced by an Oath to accuse himself, neither is it very probable, that our Saviour would have taken such an Oath. The Sense therefore seemeth to be rather I command, or require, or charge thee, as Solemnly as if thou hadst taken an Oath (as in the presence of God) to tell us. Or I charge thee with a terrible imprecation on thee, if thou speakest falsely, or wilt be silent to declare, if thou be the Christ the Son of the living God.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="64">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:271" />64 Jesus saith unto him, Thou hast said. Ne<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vertheless I say unto you, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 110.1.</ns0:note> Hereafter shall ye see the Son of Man, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 16.27. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 24.30. Rom. 14.10. 1 Thes. 4.16. Rev. 1.7.</ns0:note> sitting on the right hand of po<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wer, and coming in the clouds of heaven.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark, Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.62. saith, <ns0:hi>And Iesus said, I am, and you shall see, &c. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>And he said unto them, If I tell you, you will not believe. And if I also ask you, you will not An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swer me, nor let me go. Hereafter shall the Son of Man sit on the Right Hand of the Power of God.</ns0:hi> What all the <ns0:hi>Evan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gelists</ns0:hi> say, put together, makes up our Saviours perfect Answer. To what purpose (saith <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi>) should I Answer you? This is now but a Captious question, not propounded by you to that end that you might be satisfied as to the Truth, but only to ensnare me, for if I should tell you I <ns0:hi>am, you would not believe it.</ns0:hi> If I should argue the matter with you, you would give me no Answer. I have given you Proof enough, but yet, <ns0:hi>Caiaphas,</ns0:hi> thou hast said the Truth, I am the Christ, the Son of the ever Living blessed God, and to confirm you further; Hereafter you shall see me, whom you think to be no more than the <ns0:hi>Son of Man, sitting on the right hand of the Power of God, and com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing in the Clouds of Heaven.</ns0:hi> There is a time for a Man to speak, and a time for him to hold his Peace: In the matter of <ns0:hi>Confession of Truth.</ns0:hi> The seasons for Silence, or Speech, are to be judged from the Honour and Glory of God; when we cannot be silent without betraying the Truth, we are bound to speak. Our Lord therefore, being so solemnly adjured in the Name of God, to tell them what was the Truth; now Confesseth, and de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nieth not, that he was the Son of God, and tells them, <ns0:hi>Here<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />after</ns0:hi> they should see it, whither the term <ns0:hi>Hereafter,</ns0:hi> refers to the time soon following (as <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> in this Evangelist, and <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, in <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> seem to signifie) and be to be understood of Christ's Resurrection, his Ascen<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ion into Heaven, the coming of the Holy Ghost, and the carrying of the Gospel to all Nations, or to the day of Judgment (which the New Testament often speaks of, as a thing at hand, and that Phrase <ns0:hi>coming in the Clouds of Heaven,</ns0:hi> seems rather to signifie) or (as others think) to both, referring the <ns0:hi>sitting on the right hand of Power,</ns0:hi> to the former, and the <ns0:hi>Coming in the Clouds</ns0:hi> to the latter, is hard to determine.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="65">65 Then the high priest rent his cloths, saying, He hath spoken blasphemy, what further need have we of witnesses? Behold, now ye have hea<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>d his b<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>asphemy.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="66">66 What think ye? They answered, and said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Lev. 2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 16.</ns0:note> He is guilty of death.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath much the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.63, 64. only he saith, <ns0:hi>They Condemned him, to be Guilty of Death. Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 22.70, 71. saith, <ns0:hi>Then said they all, Art thou then the Son of God. And he said unto them, ye say that I am? And they said, what need we any further Witness? For we our selves have heard of his own Mouth.</ns0:hi> This rending of Cloths was a thing very ordinary amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> used by them, in Te<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stimony of <ns0:hi>Sorrow,</ns0:hi> and of <ns0:hi>Indignation</ns0:hi>: They used it in Causes of great Sorrow, and Mourning, even before the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> were formed into a Nation; we find it Practised by <ns0:hi>Reuben</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iacob, Gen.</ns0:hi> 37.29.34. and by <ns0:hi>Iacobs Sons, Gen.</ns0:hi> 44.13. by <ns0:hi>Ioshua,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Caleb, Numb.</ns0:hi> 14.6. by <ns0:hi>Iephtah, Iud.</ns0:hi> 11.35. indeed he that was <ns0:hi>High Priest,</ns0:hi> was <ns0:hi>forbidden</ns0:hi> to do it, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 21.10. and in Order to it, to come near a dead Body, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 11. which Command, yet the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> restrain to his <ns0:hi>Priestly Garments,</ns0:hi> but upon other occasions he might rend his Cloths, as <ns0:hi>Caiphas</ns0:hi> here did. It was usual in Case of <ns0:hi>Blasphemy,</ns0:hi> both to shew their Sorrow for it, and Detestation of it, 2 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 19.1. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 36.24. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 14.14. So as they Convicted our Saviour, not upon <ns0:hi>Oaths of Witnesses,</ns0:hi> b<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t upon Words which they interpreted to be <ns0:hi>Blasphemy.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>High Priest,</ns0:hi> being but the <ns0:hi>President</ns0:hi> in this Councel, asks the Opinion of the rest of the Councel. They all condemn him as Guilty of a Capital Crime, which is here Phrased <ns0:hi>Guilty of Death</ns0:hi>; that is, one who by their Law ought to dye.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="67">67 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap 27.30.</ns0:note> Then did they spit in his face, and buffeted him, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 19.3.</ns0:note> others smote <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> with the <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> palms of their hands.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="68">68 Saying, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 22.64.</ns0:note> Prophesie to us, thou Christ, Who is he that smote thee.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath much the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.65. <ns0:hi>And some began to spit on him, and to cover his Face, and to buffet him, and to say unto him, P<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ophesie: And the Servants did strike him with the Palms of their hands.</ns0:hi> Tho there be nothing more Barba<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rous, and Inhumane, than to add to the Affliction of the afflict<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed; yet this is no more, than we ordinarily see done by a Rabble of brutish People; spitting in the Face, was but an ordinary To<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken of Contempt, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 12.14. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 25.9. And perhaps in all these Indignities, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> was a Type of Christ, <ns0:hi>Is.</ns0:hi> 50.6. if that Text be not to be understood of Christ immediately. In the mean time it lets us see, that there is no Degree, or Mark of C<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tempt<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> or Shame, or Suffering, which we ought to decline, and Grudge at, for the Name of Christ; who tho much more Excellent than us<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> yet for our sake endured the Cross, and <ns0:hi>Despised the Shame.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="69">69 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 18 16.25.</ns0:note> Now Peter sate without in the palace, and a damsel came unto him, saying, Thou also wast with Jesus of Galilee.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="70">70 But he denied before them all, saying, I know not what thou sayest.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath this, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.66, 67. only he saith, <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> was <ns0:hi>be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />neath in the Palace,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>warming himself. Luke</ns0:hi> hath this whole Story before, what he saith of Christ's <ns0:hi>Examination, and Condemnation, Ch.</ns0:hi> 22.56. <ns0:hi>And a certain Maid beh<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ld him, as he sate by the F<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>re, and earnestly lookt upon him, and said, This Man was also with him. And he denied him, saying, Woman, I know him not.</ns0:hi> We before left <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>High Priests Palace, warming himself by the Fire amongst the Servants.</ns0:hi> It is a dangerous thing for Christians, to come into places of <ns0:hi>Tempta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion.</ns0:hi> A Maid comes to him, and Chargeth him to have been with Christ, whom she calls <ns0:hi>Iesus of Galilee</ns0:hi>: So they called Christ, sometimes <ns0:hi>Iesus of Nazareth,</ns0:hi> the City in <ns0:hi>Galilee</ns0:hi> where Christ lived the greatest part of his Life: <ns0:hi>He denied before them all</ns0:hi>: So loud that all heard it. <ns0:hi>I know not what thou sayest,</ns0:hi> or (as <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith) <ns0:hi>I know him not, I neither know him, nor what thou sayest.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="71">71 And when he was gone out into the porch, another <ns0:hi>maid</ns0:hi> saw him, and said unto them that were there, This <ns0:hi>fellow</ns0:hi> was also with Jesus of Nazareth.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="72">72 And again he denied with an oath, I do not know the man.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 70. more shortly. So <ns0:hi>Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 22.58. It is like <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> upon the first Alarm, began to shift away, and was got into the Porch, but there another meets him, with the same Charge. Here to the former lye which he had told, and here repeateth, he adds an Oath for the Confirmation of what he had said. What are the best of Men, when God leaves them to their own strength? But the Temptation, yet riseth higher.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="73">73 And after a while came unto him they that stood by, and said unto Peter. Surely thou also art <ns0:hi>one</ns0:hi> of them, for thy speech bewrayeth thee.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="74">74 Then began he to curse, and to swear, <ns0:hi>saying,</ns0:hi> I know not the man. And immediately the cock crew.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark, Ch.</ns0:hi> 14. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 70, 71. saith, <ns0:hi>And a little after, they that stood by, said again to Peter. Surely thou art one of them, for thou art a Galilean, and thy Speech agreeth thereto. But he began to Curse and to Swear, saying, I know not the Man of whom you speak, Luke</ns0:hi> hath it, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 22.59, 60. <ns0:hi>And about the space of an hour after, Another Confidently affirmed, saying, Of a Truth this fellow also was with him, for he is a Galilean. And Peter said: Man I know not what thou say<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>st. And immediately the Cock crew.</ns0:hi> One spake in the Name of the rest, that were gathered about <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> and he Chargeth <ns0:hi>Peter Confidently,</ns0:hi> and he might well, for <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 18.26. <ns0:hi>That this was one of the Servants of the High Priests, being his Kinsman, whose Ear Peter cut off,</ns0:hi> he said, <ns0:hi>Did no<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> I see thee in the Garden with him</ns0:hi>? Temptations always grow upon us, in the Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pany of wicked Men. Here <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> adds to his <ns0:hi>Lying, Swearing,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Cursing</ns0:hi>; all Confirming of what he had said, in the denial of his Master. All in an exact fulfilling of what Christ had told <ns0:hi>Peter, v.</ns0:hi> 54. tho he was then Difficult to believe it, to teach us all, not to presume too far upon our own strength, but to <ns0:hi>Pray,</ns0:hi> that we be not led into <ns0:hi>Temptation.</ns0:hi> While we stand to take heed lest we fall, and in Order to it, to avoid the Society of wicked Men, and places in which we probably may be Tempted. To teach us also Charity to lapsed Brethren, and not too ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stily to Condemn our Brethren, for falling a second and a third time, into the same sin; especially, while the same fit of Temp<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tation holdeth. It is added, <ns0:hi>and immediately the Cock crew</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> That is, the second time: So saith <ns0:hi>Mark, Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.72. who had mentioned the <ns0:hi>Cocks</ns0:hi> first Crowing, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 68. upon <ns0:hi>Peters</ns0:hi> first de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nial of his Master.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="75">75 And Peter remembred the word of Jesus, which said unto him, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Verse 3<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Mark 14.32 John<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 13.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. And he went out and wept bitterly.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 14.72. <ns0:hi>And the second time, the Cock crew, and Peter called to mind the Words, that Iesus had said unto him: Before the Cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice; and when he thought thereon he wept. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 22.61. <ns0:hi>And the Lord turned, and lookt upon Peter, and Peter remembred the Word of the Lord, how he had said unto him, Before the Cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. And Peter went out and wept bitterly.</ns0:hi> We have in this last Verse <ns0:hi>Peters</ns0:hi> Repentance, and the Occasion and Cause of it. A good Man may fall, and that foully, but he shall not fall, so as to rise no more: <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> lay longer than <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> under the Guilt of his sin, but bo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>h of them <ns0:hi>wept bitterly.</ns0:hi> He went out of the <ns0:hi>Porch,</ns0:hi> whither he went is not said, possibly he was afraid, to what this Detection of him might rise, or else sought a place (as <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> did) to weep more privately, and plentifully than be durst do, or thought convenient to do in the <ns0:hi>Porch</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>High Priest.</ns0:hi> That which gave occasion to this <ns0:hi>Reflection,</ns0:hi> was the <ns0:hi>Crowing of the Cock the second time,</ns0:hi> and his <ns0:hi>Remembrance of the Words of Iesus, v.</ns0:hi> 34. Our Memories serve us much in the business of <ns0:hi>Repentance,</ns0:hi> and therefore, that the Soul should be without knowledge of the Law of God, is not good. <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> remembred what Christ had personally said to him. True <ns0:hi>Peniten<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>s</ns0:hi> are still excited to <ns0:hi>Repentance,</ns0:hi> by remembring the Law of God, what Christ hath in his Word said to them; and considering their own ways: The Crowing of the <ns0:hi>Cock</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>second time,</ns0:hi> hel<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t him to remember the Words of Jesus, for he had said, <ns0:hi>Before the Cock crow twice,</ns0:hi> &c. But the <ns0:hi>Cause</ns0:hi> of his Repentance, is ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pressed by <ns0:hi>Luke: The Lord turned, and looked upon Peter.</ns0:hi> More must be understood by this <ns0:hi>Look of Christ</ns0:hi> upon him, then the meer cast of Christ's <ns0:hi>bodily Eye,</ns0:hi> with that Look there was a Vertue which went from Christ, which healed <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> exciting his Habit of Grace, and assisting him in the Exercise of it, which double influence of Grace, is necessary to every renewed Soul. Christ lookt upon <ns0:hi>Iudas, when Iudas kissed him:</ns0:hi> Yea, and said to him, <ns0:hi>Iudas betrayest thou the Son of Man with a kiss?</ns0:hi> Yet, <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> went on in his Villany without Remorse. He lookt up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> and he went out and <ns0:hi>wept bitterly.</ns0:hi> He lookt only upon the Face of <ns0:hi>Iudas,</ns0:hi> but he lookt upon the Heart of <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> as well as upon his Face.</ns0:note>
